companies.name: Anemoy
companies.description: Anemoy is a web3-native asset manager, founded 2023, operating as an affiliated asset-management vehicle built on the Centrifuge protocol, tokenizing and distributing real-world-asset funds (short-term Treasuries via the Janus Henderson Anemoy Treasury Fund / JTRSY, and private/direct credit via the Anemoy Tokenized Apollo Diversified Credit Fund / ACRDX) for institutional on-chain access.

criteria.rationale: Anemoy launched a second distinct fund (ACRDX, 2025) after its first (JTRSY, 2024), and secured a concrete $50 million anchor investment from a named institutional counterparty (Grove) into ACRDX -- real, dated capital committed by an actual customer of the product, not a projection. This is genuine but limited evidence: it reflects two sequential product launches and one flagship anchor commitment, not a multi-period usage series across a broad customer base.
criteria.evidenceGapNote: No dated AUM series or broader investor-count data exists beyond the single Grove anchor commitment and the two product-launch dates.

citedClaims.claim: Janus Henderson announced (September 13, 2024) a partnership with Anemoy and Centrifuge to launch the Janus Henderson Anemoy Liquid Treasury Fund (later branded JTRSY), a fully on-chain tokenized fund providing investors direct access to short-term U.S. Treasury bills; Anemoy, founded 2023 by Martin Quensel (also a Centrifuge co-founder) and Anil Sood, is described as functioning as an asset-management vehicle advancing Centrifuge's RWA product efforts and manages the fund's on-chain origination, tokenization, and distribution lifecycle, while Janus Henderson manages day-to-day fund operations through its Tabula subsidiary.

Grove (an institutional-grade credit-infrastructure protocol in the Sky Ecosystem) deployed $50 million as an anchor investment (announced September 16, 2025) into the Anemoy Tokenized Apollo Diversified Credit Fund (ACRDX), a feeder fund providing tokenized access to Apollo's diversified global credit strategy; the fund launched with Centrifuge (tokenization infrastructure) and Plume (RWA-focused settlement blockchain, distributing the strategy as nACRDX via its Nest Credit vaults), with Chronicle as oracle provider and Wormhole for cross-chain connectivity. Anemoy is named as the fund's asset manager, subject to regulatory approval.
citedClaims.diligenceQuestion: Has the stated regulatory approval for Anemoy to act as ACRDX's asset manager been obtained, and on what timeline?

criteria.rationale: Anemoy's role as ACRDX's asset manager is explicitly disclosed as "subject to regulatory approval," a concrete, real gating condition standing between announcement and full operation, with no later source confirming that approval was obtained. This is genuine friction evidence, distinct from ordinary investor-onboarding detail, which is not otherwise documented.
criteria.evidenceGapNote: Confirmation of the regulatory approval referenced for Anemoy's ACRDX asset-manager role was not found (gap-anemoy-acrdx-regulatory-approval-status).

citedClaims.claim: Grove (an institutional-grade credit-infrastructure protocol in the Sky Ecosystem) deployed $50 million as an anchor investment (announced September 16, 2025) into the Anemoy Tokenized Apollo Diversified Credit Fund (ACRDX), a feeder fund providing tokenized access to Apollo's diversified global credit strategy; the fund launched with Centrifuge (tokenization infrastructure) and Plume (RWA-focused settlement blockchain, distributing the strategy as nACRDX via its Nest Credit vaults), with Chronicle as oracle provider and Wormhole for cross-chain connectivity. Anemoy is named as the fund's asset manager, subject to regulatory approval.
citedClaims.diligenceQuestion: Has the stated regulatory approval for Anemoy to act as ACRDX's asset manager been obtained, and on what timeline?

criteria.rationale: Anemoy's tokenization infrastructure depends entirely on the Centrifuge protocol, and the unresolved public question over whether Centrifuge Network Foundation holds equity in Anemoy or whether CFG holders have any claim on its revenue leaves the economic terms of that platform dependency genuinely undocumented. An unresolved dependency on a single external protocol/brand relationship, with no established economic or governance terms between the two, is a real counterparty/platform-concentration exposure for Anemoy's own defensibility, tempered by the fact that both flagship products have shipped and operate today regardless of how that question is eventually resolved.
criteria.evidenceGapNote: The economic and governance terms of Anemoy's dependency on the Centrifuge protocol/brand remain unresolved (gap-anemoy-cfg-value-capture); no switching-cost or fork-resistance evidence exists distinct from this dependency.

citedClaims.claim: In a Centrifuge governance-forum thread dated August 23, 2026, a community member (Inflecta) publicly asked whether Centrifuge Network Foundation holds equity in Anemoy and whether CFG token holders have any direct or indirect economic claim on Anemoy's economics, framing this against a governance proposal (CP-171) that asserted CFG as Centrifuge's "single value accrual mechanism." As of the thread's most recent visible reply (same day), neither question had been answered by Centrifuge team members or moderators.
citedClaims.diligenceQuestion: Does the Centrifuge Network Foundation hold equity in Anemoy, and do CFG token holders have any direct or indirect economic claim on Anemoy's revenue?

citedClaims.claim: ChainSecurity audited Chronicle's Scribe oracle mechanism ahead of its September 2023 public launch. The audit's stated scope covered functional correctness, integration of the signature scheme, and access control (plus code complexity, external-system integration, and documentation quality); the Schnorr signature scheme's underlying cryptography was explicitly excluded from scope. Three issues were identified (stale poke-data on update; finalized-status assessment after an authenticated action; unreset op-poke-data after an unsuccessful challenge), all of which were resolved or acknowledged by the Chronicle team. ChainSecurity's stated conclusion was that "the codebase provides a good level of security," not that the protocol is secure without qualification.

companies.name: Lava Network
companies.description: Lava Network is a decentralized RPC/data-access protocol that routes application, exchange, and AI-agent traffic to independent data providers across many blockchains, incentivized and secured by the LAVA token.

criteria.rationale: The only usage-adoption evidence is Lava's own July 2024 claim of "50+ billion RPC requests across 30+ networks," which the packet records as evidenceStatus insufficient: it is company-sourced, does not specify the measurement period, and cannot be attributed to testnet versus mainnet activity. It is cited here for completeness but does not support a directional momentum judgment.
criteria.evidenceGapNote: No independently corroborated, dated usage/transaction figure exists (gap-lava-network-metrics); secondary aggregator figures (e.g., "40 million monthly active users") were deliberately excluded by the research packet as insufficiently sourced.

citedClaims.claim: Lava's own July 31, 2024 launch-retrospective blog post states the network "handled 50+ billion RPC requests across 30+ networks" without specifying the exact measurement period or whether this spans the testnet phase, the mainnet period, or both.
citedClaims.diligenceQuestion: What time period does the 50+ billion RPC request figure actually cover, and can it be independently corroborated?

criteria.rationale: No claim documents onboarding friction, audit/compliance requirements, or ecosystem reachability for Lava's RPC/data-access infrastructure.
criteria.evidenceGapNote: No adoption-friction or ecosystem-access evidence exists in the frozen packet.

criteria.rationale: The same centralized-control fact relevant to governance (Foundation as sole controller of token sales and roadmap, transition to DAO unconfirmed) also bears on durability: concentrated control is a structural weakness for a network effect thesis premised on decentralization. No claim documents validator/provider-base size, audit history, or liquidity/retention data that would offset this.
criteria.evidenceGapNote: No validator/provider-base size, audit history, or liquidity-retention evidence exists in the frozen packet (gap-lava-decentralization).

citedClaims.claim: As of the May 2024 Foundation token round, The Block reported the Lava Foundation as "the sole entity that sells tokens and decides the roadmap for the network until the DAO is live at mainnet," indicating centralized control of token sales and roadmap decisions pending a stated future transition to DAO governance.
citedClaims.diligenceQuestion: Has the described DAO transition actually occurred, and what is the current on-chain governance/control structure?

criteria.rationale: No claim addresses developer, contributor, or third-party integration growth for Lava Network.
criteria.evidenceGapNote: No developer or ecosystem-integration evidence exists in the frozen packet.

criteria.rationale: No claim documents a developer self-serve motion, repeatable enterprise/protocol sales channel, or composability-driven integration pull, distinct from the network's own unverified request-volume claim.
criteria.evidenceGapNote: No distribution or integration-pull evidence exists in the frozen packet.

criteria.rationale: The $2M in initial network incentives paid alongside the mainnet airdrop is evidence the network relied on a funded subsidy to bootstrap at launch. No data exists on whether this reliance has tapered or whether contribution economics hold without continued incentive spend.
criteria.evidenceGapNote: No post-launch burn, contribution-margin, or token-sale-reliance data exists in the frozen packet.

citedClaims.claim: Lava Network launched its public mainnet ("Eruption") on July 30, 2024, with a community-first airdrop of 55 million LAVA tokens to roughly 70,000 users and $2 million in initial network incentives.

criteria.rationale: As of the May 2024 Foundation token round, independent journalism reported the Lava Foundation as "the sole entity that sells tokens and decides the roadmap for the network until the DAO is live at mainnet"; no later source confirms that transition occurred (gap-lava-dao-transition-status). A subsequent on-chain governance vote extended the token lockup for stakeholders by one year in a close vote reportedly supported by the same major holders whose tokens it locks, a change whose investor-protective versus protocol-protective motivation is not established. Together this is evidence of concentrated, unconfirmed-transition control, tempered by the fact that governance is at least conducted through visible on-chain proposals rather than opaquely.

companies.name: Morpho Labs
companies.description: Morpho is a decentralized, noncustodial lending infrastructure stack for permissionless isolated markets and curated vaults. Morpho Labs is a development company associated with the protocol; a French nonprofit, Morpho Association, supports protocol development and hosts an interface; MORPHO token holders govern a limited set of protocol parameters.

criteria.rationale: Morpho reports users increasing from 67,000 to more than 1.4 million and deposits from $5 billion to $13 billion during 2025, providing favorable temporal direction. Both series are first-party, not independently verified, and lack user-definition and retention methodology.
criteria.evidenceGapNote: Independent measurement, deduplication, retained cohorts, and repeat-borrowing data are unavailable.

citedClaims.claim: Morpho reported that its user count rose from 67,000 to more than 1.4 million during 2025.
citedClaims.diligenceQuestion: Provide methodology, deduplication, active-use threshold, and cohort retention for the reported user count.

citedClaims.claim: Morpho reported that deposits increased from $5 billion to $13 billion during 2025.
citedClaims.diligenceQuestion: Reconcile gross deposits, TVL methodology, rehypothecated positions, and chain-level duplication.

criteria.rationale: Permissionless isolated-market creation and a live Coinbase interface provide concrete ecosystem-access paths, supporting limited favorable direction. The frozen evidence does not quantify onboarding, integration, wallet, oracle, or collateral friction.
criteria.evidenceGapNote: Implementation time, rejection or failure rates, and end-user onboarding friction are unavailable.

citedClaims.claim: Morpho Protocol permits creation of immutable, isolated lending markets with market-specific collateral, loan asset, oracle, interest-rate model, and liquidation LTV parameters.
Coinbase launched Bitcoin-backed USDC loans on January 16, 2025 using Morpho markets on Base.

criteria.rationale: Morpho's first-party postmortem documents a vulnerability serious enough to pause supply, although it was responsibly disclosed and patched without a documented theft. An independent ChainSecurity audit also identified a scoped data-structure insufficiency and cautioned that audits cannot find every vulnerability, supporting modest adverse security direction rather than broad safety or defensibility claims.
criteria.evidenceGapNote: Later-deployment audit coverage, complete incident history, switching costs, and durable network effects remain incomplete.

citedClaims.claim: A June 2023 disclosed Aave V3 Optimizer vulnerability could have enabled theft through manipulated pool indexes; Morpho paused supply, patched the issue, and paid a $285,000 bounty after responsible disclosure.

companies.name: Nillion
companies.description: Nillion is a "blind computation" privacy-infrastructure network (branded "Petnet"), combining multi-party computation (MPC) and other privacy-enhancing technologies to let applications process data without revealing its contents. Nillion launched its own Cosmos-based mainnet ("nilChain") in March 2025, then announced in January 2026 a migration to Ethereum ("Nillion 2.0"), redefining NIL's role around staking, node-operator access, and payments on Ethereum rather than governance of a standalone chain.

criteria.rationale: No usage, transaction, or node-operator-count evidence exists. A July 2025 "Phase 0" upgrade announcement that might have contained capacity or usage detail could not be opened and reviewed during research and was deliberately excluded rather than cited on weak provenance.
criteria.evidenceGapNote: No usage/network-activity metric exists (gap-nillion-network-metrics); the Phase 0 upgrade announcement was inaccessible and excluded (gap-nillion-phase0-upgrade-detail).

criteria.rationale: Operating a "Blacklight" verification node under the Nillion 2.0 design requires staking 70,000 NIL, a concrete, quantified capital barrier to that specific participation role. This is real friction evidence for node operators, though it says nothing about end-user onboarding friction (wallet UX, compliance, liquidity access).
criteria.evidenceGapNote: No end-user-facing friction evidence (wallet UX, compliance, liquidity access) exists; only node-operator capital friction is documented.

citedClaims.claim: Nillion announced on January 27, 2026 that it is migrating its network architecture from a Cosmos-based chain ("nilChain") to Ethereum, rebranded "Nillion 2.0," redefining NIL from primarily a governance/staking token on its own chain to a token required for access, staking (including a stated 70,000 NIL requirement to operate a "Blacklight" verification node launching February 2, 2026), and peer-to-peer payments on Ethereum. Kraken's exchange support documentation (last updated February 27, 2026) independently confirmed the migration was underway, scheduling a Cosmos deposit/ withdrawal pause (March 13, 2026) and a client migration window (March 16-20, 2026) with balances converted 1:1.
citedClaims.diligenceQuestion: Has the migration completed as scheduled (nilChain halt around March 23, 2026, per secondary reporting not independently confirmed here), and what portion of total NIL supply has actually bridged to Ethereum?

criteria.rationale: No confirmed, admissible-standard security audit exists for either the NIL token contract or the core MPC network contracts (gap-nillion-audit-scope: secondary sources mention a Quantstamp audit but no dated, admissible source was found). Separately, a large, uncontrolled NIL token sale by a market-facing counterparty occurred in November 2025, causing a roughly 50% price crash; this is direct evidence of a real access/market-control weakness at that point in the network's history, regardless of how the "unauthorized" characterization is ultimately resolved. No claim documents a validator/node-operator base size or observed resistance to forks that would offset this.
criteria.evidenceGapNote: No confirmed audit exists (gap-nillion-audit-scope); no validator/node-base-size or liquidity-retention data exists (gap-nillion-network-metrics).

citedClaims.claim: On or around November 20, 2025, an unauthorized market maker sold a large quantity of NIL tokens without authorization from the Nillion Association, causing NIL to crash roughly 50% (from above $0.21 to an intraday low near $0.086-0.092) on a 680% spike in daily volume; Nillion stated it deployed treasury funds for buybacks, worked with exchanges to freeze associated accounts, and pursued legal action.
citedClaims.diligenceQuestion: Was the counterparty market maker's authorization status confirmed by any party other than Nillion, and what was the outcome of the stated legal action?

companies.name: Notabene
companies.description: Notabene, Inc. provides pre-transaction authorization, counterparty-risk and Travel Rule compliance software for digital-asset businesses and financial institutions, and develops products using the open Transaction Authorization Protocol.

criteria.rationale: Company-reported platform scale rose from more than 20 customers in 2021 to more than 165 by November 2024 and more than 190 through year end, alongside more than 32 million compliant transfers. The multi-period comparative evidence supports favorable adoption momentum, while its first-party provenance and missing retention and active-customer measures constrain certainty rather than erase direction.
criteria.evidenceGapNote: Independent metric verification, retention cohorts, churn, and the active-customer share were not established.

citedClaims.claim: At the Series A announcement, Notabene reported more than 20 platform customers, including Luno, Bitso, Paxful and Crypto.com, and said more than 50 exchanges had processed Travel Rule transactions with its solution.

At the November 2024 Series B announcement, Notabene reported more than 165 companies on its platform across more than 80 jurisdictions and nearly $500 billion of customer transaction volume processed.
Notabene's year-end review reported more than 32 million compliant transfers across more than 85 jurisdictions and more than 190 customers during or through 2024.

criteria.rationale: Company-controlled materials describe protocol-agnostic compliance tooling and a blockchain-neutral pre-settlement authorization protocol using signed requests and DIDComm. These designs are relevant to ecosystem reach and integration workflow, but no onboarding time, implementation burden, or comparative friction evidence establishes direction.
criteria.evidenceGapNote: Integration time, compliance implementation burden, onboarding failure rates, and comparative access were not established.

citedClaims.claim: In 2021 Notabene described a protocol-agnostic suite for counterparty-risk management and privacy-preserving exchange of customer data to support Travel Rule compliance.

TAP defines signed pre-settlement transfer requests, DIDComm messaging and policy coordination so wallets, exchanges, institutions and smart contracts can authorize blockchain payments before funds move, without tying settlement to one blockchain.

criteria.rationale: Notabene reported a clean SOC 2 Type II result, and an independent directory lists SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 compliance. This supports limited favorable security-posture evidence, but the underlying reports, auditor, periods, and renewal dates were unavailable; attestations do not prove no incidents or establish switching costs or network effects.
criteria.evidenceGapNote: Public report scope, current audit periods, incident history, switching costs, participant concentration, and network effects were not established.

citedClaims.claim: Notabene announced a clean SOC 2 Type II report covering security and privacy in January 2022; a later independent directory lists Notabene as SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 compliant but does not publish the auditor, report period or renewal date.

criteria.rationale: TAP specifications and code exist, but their existence does not establish external contributor growth, third-party developer expansion, or adoption of TAP independent of Notabene products.
criteria.evidenceGapNote: Related protocol and code evidence exists, but external contributors, integrations, and ecosystem growth were not established.

criteria.rationale: Company-reported customer growth from more than 20 in 2021 to more than 165 in 2024 provides temporal evidence of repeatable distribution, while Copper independently announced an integration for its institutional clients. companies.name: Pixels
companies.description: Pixels is a farming/exploration-themed multiplayer on-chain game, currently built on Sky Mavis' Ronin blockchain, with an associated PIXEL governance and reward token used for staking, ecosystem rewards, and in-game economy.

criteria.rationale: Pixels self-reported surpassing 1 million DAU in May 2024, but independent on-chain analytics (ChainArgos) and third-party commentary two weeks later estimated roughly 70% of Pixels-linked Ronin accounts were bots, with a growth curve "too smooth" for organic activity; the company's own developers acknowledged the problem by banning 750,000 accounts in a single week, though bot activity reportedly rebounded afterward. Reported daily-active-account counts are not equated with durable human user adoption per this criterion's evidentiary standard; the credible, sourced bot-contamination finding materially undercuts any claim of real, persisting usage momentum from this period.

citedClaims.claim: Pixels stated in early-to-mid May 2024 that it had surpassed 1 million daily active users, a self-reported company claim covered by The Block, with the CEO separately citing a 30-day PIXEL-token spend-to-distribution ratio (4.4 million PIXEL spent, ~$1.6 million) as a supporting metric; The Block's coverage does not independently verify the 1 million figure.
citedClaims.contradictionNote: Independent reporting two weeks later estimated roughly 70% of Pixels accounts on Ronin were bots, directly undermining the reliability (though not necessarily the entire premise) of the 1 million DAU claim.
citedClaims.diligenceQuestion: What share of the claimed 1 million DAU reflects genuine distinct human users versus automated/bot wallets?

citedClaims.claim: Independent reporting (Cointelegraph Magazine, May 27, 2024) cited on-chain analytics firm ChainArgos finding the growth curve of daily unique PIXEL recipients "too smooth" for organic human activity, and quoted Eldarune CEO Can Picak estimating approximately 70% of Pixels accounts on Ronin were bots; Pixels' developers acknowledged the problem, stating they banned 750,000 accounts in a single week, though bot activity reportedly rebounded after ban waves.
citedClaims.contradictionNote: Directly undermines the reliability of the company's self-reported 1 million DAU figure from two weeks earlier.

companies.name: Skyfire
companies.description: Skyfire (skyfire.xyz) builds the "Agent Trust Stack," payment infrastructure that gives AI agents verifiable identity (the KYA / Know Your Agent protocol) and their own USDC-stablecoin or card-rail-backed wallets so they can autonomously identify themselves and transact without human intervention at time of payment.

criteria.rationale: Named early users exist (Denso, Payman at Aug 2024 launch; ~30 KYAPay launch partners reported by PYMNTS in July 2025), but both are recorded as evidenceStatus: insufficient: the launch customers were design partners with no measured usage depth, and the partner count is a company-supplied figure with no confirmation of how many reached live production use. No transaction volume, active-agent count, or growth trend exists to establish persistence rather than a point-in-time announcement.
criteria.evidenceGapNote: No quantified or time-series usage evidence exists (gap-skyfire-quantified-traction); production status of named customers/partners is unconfirmed.

citedClaims.claim: At August 2024 launch, TechCrunch reported Denso using Skyfire to let AI agents autonomously source materials, and Payman using Skyfire's platform so AI agents could hire and pay contract workers independently.
citedClaims.diligenceQuestion: What is the depth/scale of the Denso and Payman integrations, and are they still active as of the cutoff?

citedClaims.claim: Skyfire launched the open KYAPay protocol and an "Agent Checkout" capability on or before July 14, 2025, enabling AI agents to independently sign up for accounts, log in, and pay online; PYMNTS reported roughly 30 launch partners including Apify, CarbonArc, BuildShip, and Forter, with SDK integration reported as achievable in "as little as 15 minutes."
citedClaims.diligenceQuestion: How many of the ~30 launch partners were in live production use of KYAPay as of the research cutoff, versus announced-only?

criteria.rationale: PYMNTS reported KYAPay SDK integration as achievable "in as little as 15 minutes," a concrete low-friction claim. This is a company-supplied figure relayed by an independent outlet, not independently timed or verified across the ~30 named partners, so it is treated as a modest positive signal rather than confirmed friction data.
criteria.evidenceGapNote: The stated integration time is unverified across partners; no compliance/wallet-UX friction evidence exists for end users of agent wallets.

criteria.rationale: USTB is purchasable and redeemable via USDC, a concrete mechanism detail that reduces friction relative to traditional bank-wire fund subscription/redemption. companies.description: Turnkey provides non-custodial wallet infrastructure and open-source SDKs for developers to embed crypto wallets and automate on-chain transaction signing. criteria.rationale: Two distinct, relevant facts pull in different directions. The Code4rena audit found one HIGH-severity issue whose remediation status is unconfirmed, a real security-posture gap. Separately, the Kinto default was an exploit that occurred upstream at the borrower Kinto itself, draining Kinto's own pools -- it is not a Wildcat smart-contract exploit, and this packet does not treat it as one. What is directly relevant to Wildcat's own defensibility is that its per-market, borrower-isolated design appears (per reporting) to have contained the resulting default's losses to the single affected market rather than letting it cascade protocol-wide, which is evidence the risk-isolation architecture functioned as designed under a real stress event. No claim documents validator/lender-base size or observed resistance to forks that would further support a network-effects judgment either way.

citedClaims.claim: Kinto, a borrower on the Wildcat protocol operating the "Phoenix Facility" credit market, announced it would shut down after a summer 2025 exploit drained $1.55 million from its lending pools and a subsequent $1 million recovery loan proved insufficient. At the time of the report, Wildcat had $150+ million in outstanding credit across $368 million originated since launch.
